caption:
Year 2 in business comes with a surprise bill: PAYG instalments.

What triggers it. After you lodge a return showing all three of these, the ATO enters you automatically:
- $4,000 or more of instalment income (business and investment income),
- $1,000 or more of tax payable on your latest assessment,
- $500 or more of estimated tax.

What it is. You pay the current year's tax as you go, usually each quarter, instead of one lump after you lodge.

Why it stings. In the same few months you pay last year's whole bill and start paying this year's in instalments. Nothing extra is owed overall, but the cash leaves much earlier than year one taught you to expect.

The ATO tells you through myGov, online services or a letter: when to pay, how often and how much.

Did year 2 catch you out?

Narrated by an AI voice.

#paygi #soletrader #smallbusinessaustralia #abn #taxplanning
